newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas chief seeks to calm disposals talk.
newsitem.headline: Havas chief seeks to calm disposals talk.

text.p: Pierre Dauzier, chairman of Havas, said on Friday he did not expect the French communications group to open the capital of its travel agency Havas Voyages to another shareholder in the near future.
He also told a meeting of share analysts that there was no potential partner for Havas Advertising waiting in the wings.
If Havas were to cut its stake in its advertising unit to allow a partnership, it would be with a view to building it up again later, he said.
Dauzier, seeking to quash rumours over what Havas might do with the two units following its February accord with Cie Generale des Eaux, said, "We will not separate from Havas Advertising".
He reiterated that Havas would be prepared to reduce its stake in Havas Advertising to allow its unit to take on a partner which could help its international development.
But Havas would view this in the same way that it had seen Canal Plus's merger with Nethold, in which it had reduced its stake in Canal Plus to allow the merger to go ahead.
Havas would then envisage rebuilding its stake gradually, as it is doing with Canal Plus, Dauzier said, adding that Canal Plus was central to Havas.
Havas Advertising served Havas as a window on consumer behaviour and the behaviour of enterprises, he said. "Havas Advertising can be a permanent source of information to us."

He did not rule out opening the capital of Havas Voyages to another shareholder, but said Havas was constrained in this by an accord with American Express on business travel which runs for another two or three years.
"I am not closing the door to a possible opening of Havas Voyages' capital, but this would have to be done calmly and over time," he said.
